Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
The lion sees the lion.

Predicates:
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
Sees($x, $y, bool) ::: Does x see y?
Likes($x, $y, bool) ::: Does x like y?
Visits($x, $y, bool) ::: Does x visit y?
Round($x, bool) ::: Is x round?
Red($x, bool) ::: Is x red?
Big($x, bool) ::: Is x big?

Facts:
Young(Cow, True) ::: The cow is young.
Sees(Cow, Lion, True) ::: The cow sees the lion.
Likes(Dog, Cow, True) ::: The dog likes the cow.
Likes(Dog, Rabbit, True) ::: The dog likes the rabbit.
Sees(Dog, Rabbit, True) ::: The dog sees the rabbit.
Young(Lion, True) ::: The lion is young.
Sees(Lion, Cow, True) ::: The lion sees the cow.
Sees(Lion, Dog, True) ::: The lion sees the dog.
Sees(Lion, Rabbit, True) ::: The lion sees the rabbit.
Round(Rabbit, True) ::: The rabbit is round.
Likes(Rabbit, Cow, True) ::: The rabbit likes the cow.

Rules:
Visits($x, Rabbit, True) >>> Likes(Rabbit, Lion, True) ::: If someone visits the rabbit then the rabbit likes the lion.
Likes($x, Rabbit, True) && Red(Rabbit, True) >>> Big(Rabbit, True) ::: If someone likes the rabbit and the rabbit is red then the rabbit is big.
Likes($x, Lion, True) && Sees($x, Rabbit, True) >>> Likes(Lion, Rabbit, True) ::: If someone likes the lion and they see the rabbit then the lion likes the rabbit.
Young($x, True) >>> Likes($x, Rabbit, True) ::: If someone is young then they like the rabbit.
Young($x, True) >>> Sees($x, Lion, True) ::: If someone is young then they see the lion.
Big(Lion, True) >>> Visits(Lion, Dog, True) ::: If the lion is big then the lion visits the dog.
Likes(Rabbit, Lion, True) >>> Young(Rabbit, True) ::: If the rabbit likes the lion then the rabbit is young.
Young($x, True) && Likes($x, Rabbit, True) >>> Visits($x, Rabbit, True) ::: If someone is young and they like the rabbit then they visit the rabbit.

Query:
Sees(Lion, Lion, True) ::: The lion sees the lion.
